focusedAudit.reason: A Beta patch release over beta.2. New surfaces (multi-window, tray, Flatpak, theming) were verified per batch with real-app journeys; storage changes (G26, G37) are per-batch fixes. No exact-tree release audit was run for this Beta; that is an explicit deferral, not an audit certification.

items.text: Linux: each Beta release now includes an installable **Flatpak** bundle, `Tine-Beta_<version>_x86_64.flatpak` (`flatpak install --user` the downloaded file). It uses the Beta identity (`page.tine.TineBeta`), so it installs beside a stable Tine Flatpak with its own data, includes the library the system tray needs, and is updated by installing the next bundle by hand (its update notice offers the download instead of trying to install in place). The release workflow builds it with the other platforms and a failed Flatpak build blocks the release.

items.text: Desktop: optional system-tray icon. Settings → Appearance adds **Show Tine in the system tray** (menu: Open Tine, Quick Capture, Quit), **Minimize to tray** (minimizing the main window hides it instead of leaving it in the taskbar) and **Start minimized to tray** (launch with the main window hidden, graph already loaded). All three are off by default; closing the main window still quits; a desktop without a tray host keeps the window shown and says so in Settings, and a tray host that disappears while Tine runs brings the hidden window back (GH #625, UI-OG-GH625).

items.text: Desktop: **Open in new window** opens a page in a separate OS window (page right-click menu, the page title's ⋯ menu, or the command palette's **Open current page in new window**). Each window has its own tabs, splits and back/forward history, and no sidebars; edits save and undo exactly as in the main window, closing a window from its title bar keeps text typed just before, and open windows (up to 8) come back at the next launch. Switching graphs closes them. Documented in Workflows > Keep context visible (UI-OG-MULTIWINDOW).

items.text: Theming (GH #610): a documented set of **`--tine-*` tokens** for `logseq/custom.css`: `--tine-embed-bg`, `--tine-embed-accent`, `--tine-bullet-color`, `--tine-bullet-size`, `--tine-tag-color`, `--tine-highlight-bg`, `--tine-content-width`, `--tine-content-width-wide`, `--tine-page-title-size`, `--tine-font-size`, `--tine-content-font`, `--tine-mono-font` and `--tine-editable-font`. Each starts unset (declared under `:where(:root)`, so a plain `html { --tine-...: ... }` or `:root { ... }` rule in custom.css wins), nothing looks different until you set one, and Logseq's `--ls-*` colors keep working unchanged. The font tokens also apply under the editorial page Style preset, and `--tine-mono-font` reaches every monospace surface (code blocks, org timestamps, inline code, editors, diagnostics). The contract (`docs/contracts/theme-tokens.md`) promises that removing or renaming a token gets a **Changed** entry here, and a guard test fails when a documented token is missing from the CSS or a `--tine-*` name ships undocumented.

items.text: Settings → Appearance → **Custom CSS** (GH #610): **Edit custom.css** (desktop) creates the file with a commented starter if the graph has none and opens it in your editor; saving it re-applies it live in the open window, with no restart and no reopening the graph (every platform with a file watcher, no new polling); **Disable custom CSS** is a session-only safe mode so a broken stylesheet can always be recovered from; **Developer tools** (desktop, also Ctrl+Shift+J, Cmd+Shift+J on macOS) opens the inspector to see what styles an element (opened and closed again on a release build under Linux; **Disable custom CSS** is also in the command palette, so it stays reachable if a stylesheet hides Settings). **Edit custom.css** opens the file with your system's default app for `.css` files, which may not be a text editor; choose one there. If a live re-read fails, the previous stylesheet stays applied and Tine retries once before it says so; a failure at graph open applies none.

items.text: Theme gallery (GH #649): **Soft**, a medium-brightness palette. Light mode is a warm medium-light neutral and dark mode a neutral medium-dark; the whole surface system moves together (page, sidebars, tabs, menus, code blocks, borders, hover and selection, text) and every text color stays at or above 4.5:1 contrast, including text on accent-filled labels and buttons, links on the selection overlay, muted text on tertiary surfaces and the bullet and checkbox markers (3:1), checked by a test computed from the palette. Accent-filled labels read their text color from a new `--on-accent` token that only Soft defines, so the stock themes look the same.

items.text: Queries (GH #651): the Guide now says why a task nested under another matching task has no row of its own in the Table, Board or result count. Tine follows Logseq's rule, a match is dropped from the top level only when its immediate parent also matches (the List shows it inside that parent), and a match under a block that does not match, such as after narrowing the query so the parent stops matching, is its own row. Pinned for every presentation by a store test and a real-app journey; no behaviour change.

items.text: Android (GH #654): the copy button on an image (on the picture itself and in the full-screen view) always answered "Couldn't copy the image", because the system clipboard plugin Tine used cannot put an image on the Android clipboard. Tine now stages the picture in its cache and puts it on the Android clipboard through the app's own file provider, which is how Android apps share images. What could not be checked without a device is whether pasting that clipboard image into a block adds it as a picture on every Android version (UI-OG-GH654).

items.text: Opening pages: a single page whose properties were followed by a blank line and then a `#+` directive (for example `title:: X`, a blank line, `#+description: y`, or an Org file-level property drawer before `#+title:`) made every link and tag fail with "Couldn't open this page: task N panicked with message \"byte range starts at N+1 but ends at N\"" and left `[[` completion with no pages. Such pages now open and keep their title, and a page whose title cannot be read no longer stops the rest of the graph from loading (GH #644, REG-OG-GH644).

items.text: External edits: a page changed on disk (by Syncthing, Dropbox or another editor) stayed stale while one of its blocks was open in the editor, which includes leaving Tine for another app with the caret still in a block; it updated only after you pressed Escape or navigated away and back, and typing into the stale block then raised a conflict. The page now updates in place and the editor stays on the same block (found by its `id::`, else by its place in the outline), with the caret kept; if the change deleted that block the editor closes. A change still waits while text is being composed with an input method, and a different file taking the page's name is still refused while you edit (REG-OG-RELOAD-WHILE-EDITING).

items.text: Saving: a page whose unsaved text already matched the file on disk (for example because a sync tool delivered the same text) counted as saved without making that file durable, and its crash-safe copy was dropped; a power cut right after could lose the text. Such a save now flushes the file to disk before counting as saved (REG-OG-G26-EQUAL-BYTES-DURABLE).
